newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Sept CPI rises 4.7 pct yr-on-yr.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Sept CPI rises 4.7 pct yr-on-yr.

text.p: South Korea's consumer price index (CPI) rose 4.7 percent in September on the year against a 4.7 percent rise a year earlier, Ministry of Finance and Economy (MFE) figures showed on Tuesday.
A finance ministry official said the year-on-year CPI rise in September was mainly due to a jump in the prices of petroleum products in line with rising oil prices on the world market.
Petroleum product prices rose 14.5 percent September year-on-year.

But the prices of agricultural and livestock products in September fell 0.4 percent on the year due to rising supplies. These items were among the major causes for the rise in South Korean inflation, he said.
CPI rose 4.7 percent for the first nine months of this year, exceeding the government 1996 target of 4.5 percent.
But the government still remained optimistic over the 1996 inflation target.
"As we are expecting a good harvest this year, the targetted 4.5 percent inflation rise for this year will be easily met," the official said by telephone.
